comments.text:
It is not accurate to say that “Russia supported Abkhazia.” Abkhazia achieved de facto independence in 1993, and its greatest success came in September of that year/month, when Russia was busy saving its own democracy, with tanks shelling the White House in Moscow.

A few months earlier, Shevardnadze had flown to Moscow and pleaded for heavy weaponry that Georgia was not entitled to under the Tashkent Agreement. Yeltsin provided it, which helped Georgian forces capture Sukhumi in August.

Yes, there were forces within Russia that helped Abkhazia and opposed Yeltsin’s support for Shevardnadze’s regime. But it is inaccurate to say that Russia supported Abkhazia. On the contrary, Russia imposed a blockade on Abkhazia in the late 1990s, and Abkhazians still harbor resentment over that period.

Yes, the winds changed after 2005, and in 2008 Putin occupied Abkhazia. But by then, Georgia had already been out of control of the republic for 15 years.
